nodes.name: Lemma 1
nodes.statement: For any disjoint subsets $A$ and $B$ of $V$, we have $\phi(A\cup B)\le \max\left\{\phi(A),\phi(B)\right\}$. If we further assume that $E(A,B)=\varnothing$, then we have $$\min\left\{\phi(A),\phi(B)\right\} \le \phi(A\cup B)\le \max\left\{\phi(A),\phi(B)\right\}.$$

nodes.name: Lemma 2
nodes.statement: For any subpartition $(B_1,\cdots,B_k)$ of $V$, we have \[h(B_1\cup\cdots\cup B_k)\le \min\{h(B_1),\cdots,h(B_k)\}.\] If we further assume that $E(B_i,B_j)=\varnothing$ whenever $i\ne j$, then we have \[h(B_1\cup\cdots\cup B_k)=\min\{h(B_1),\cdots,h(B_k)\}.\]

nodes.name: Lemma 3
nodes.statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Suppose that \[(A_1,\dots,A_k)\text{ and }(B_1,\dots,B_{n-k+1})\] are subpartitions of $[n]:=\{1,\dots, n\}$, then there exists a nonempty subset $\{i_1,\dots,i_t\}$ of $[k]$ and a nonempty subset $\{j_1,\dots,j_s\}$ of $[n-k+1]$ such that \[A_{i_1}\cup\dots\cup A_{i_t}=B_{j_1}\cup\dots\cup B_{j_s}.\]

nodes.name: Proposition 1
nodes.statement:
For any weighted graph $G=(V,E,\mu,w)$,
$$h_k(G):=\min_{(A_1,\dots,A_{k})\in \mathcal{P}_k(V)}~\max_{1\le i\le k}\phi(A_i)=\min_{(A_1,\dots,A_{k})\in \mathcal{P}_k(V)}~\max_{B\in \mathcal{U}(A_1,\cdots,A_{k})}\phi(B)$$
where \[\mathcal{U}(A_1,\cdots,A_k):=\{A_{i_1}\cup\cdots\cup A_{i_q}:1\le i_1<\cdots<i_q\le k,\,1\le q\le k\}\] stands for the union closed family generated by the $k$-tuple of sets $(A_1,\cdots,A_k)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3
nodes.statement:
For any weighted graph $\tilde G=(\tilde V,\tilde E,\tilde\mu,\tilde w)$ with $n$ vertices, for any $k\in\{1,2,\cdots,n\}$, we have \[h_k(\tilde G)\ge \ell_k(\tilde G)\ge \underline{\ell_k}(\tilde G).\] 
For any weighted forest $G=(V,E,\mu,w)$ with $n$ vertices, we must have \[h_k(G)= \ell_k(G)= \underline{\ell_k}(G).\]

nodes.name: Theorem 4
nodes.statement: For any weighted graph $\tilde G=(\tilde V,\tilde E,\tilde\mu,\tilde w)$,  \[h_k(\tilde G)\ge \ell_k(\tilde G)\ge \underline{\ell_k}(\tilde G)\ge h_{k-\beta}(\tilde G),\] where $\beta:=|\tilde E|-|\tilde V|+c$ is the total number of independent loops of $\tilde G$, and $c$ is the number of connected components of $\tilde G$.

nodes.name: Theorem 6
nodes.statement:
For any weighted graph $G=(V,E,\mu,w)$, 
$$h_{k-\beta}(G) \le \lambda_{k}(\Delta_1)\le h_k(G),$$
where $\beta:=|E|-|V|+1$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1
nodes.statement:
For any forest $G=(V,E,\mu,w)$, we have \[\min_{\mathrm{subpartitions~}(A_1,\dots,A_{k})\mathrm{~of~}V}~~\max_{B\in \mathcal{U}(A_1,\cdots,A_{k})}\phi(B)=\max_{\mathrm{subpartitions~}(A_1,\dots,A_{n-k+1})\mathrm{~of~}V}~~\min_{B\in \mathcal{U}(A_1,\cdots,A_{n-k+1})}\phi(B),\]
where \[\mathcal{U}(A_1,\cdots,A_k)=\{A_{i_1}\cup\cdots\cup A_{i_q}:1\le i_1<\cdots<i_q\le k,\,1\le q\le k\}\] denotes the union-closed family generated by the subpartition $(A_1,\dots,A_{k})$ of $V$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5
Corollary 2
nodes.statement: For any forest $G$, we have $$\lambda_{k}^\gamma(\Delta_1)= h_k(G).$$

nodes.name: Corollary 1
nodes.statement:
Let $\Delta_1$ denote the 1-Laplacian of a forest. Then, for any $k$, 
$$ \lambda_k^{\gamma}(\Delta_1)=\lambda_k^{\gamma^+}(\Delta_1) =\lambda_k^{\textrm{Y-ind}}(\Delta_1).$$

nodes.name: Theorem 2
Lemma 4
nodes.statement:
Given a weighted graph $G=(V,E,\mu,w)$, assume that $\mu_v=\sum_{u\in V:u\sim v}w_{uv}$ for any $v\in V$. 
For any $k$, the $k$-th min-max eigenvalue $\lambda_k(\Delta_p)$ is locally Lipschitz continuous with respect to $p$, and moreover, 
\begin{itemize}
    \item the function $p\mapsto p(2\lambda_k(\Delta_p))^{\frac1p}$ 
is increasing  on $
[1,+\infty)$,
\item 
the function 
$p\mapsto2^{-p}\lambda_k(\Delta_p)$ is decreasing on $[1,+\infty)$.
\end{itemize}

nodes.name: Corollary 3
nodes.statement:
For any weighted forest $G$ satisfying $\mu_v=\sum_{u\in V:u\sim v}w_{uv}$, $\forall v\in V$, for any $p\ge 1$, we have
$$\frac{2^{p-1}}{p^p}h_k(G)^p\le \lambda_{k}(\Delta_p)\le 2^{p-1} h_k(G).$$

nodes.name: Lemma 7
Lemma 6
nodes.statement: For any $x\in \mathrm{span}(\mathbbm 1_{A_1},\cdots,\mathbbm 1_{A_{n-k+1}})\setminus\{0\}$, there exists $B\in \mathcal{U}(A_1,\cdots,A_{n-k+1})$ such that $\Phi_1(x)\ge\phi(B)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 5
nodes.statement: For any linear subspace $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ of dimension $n-k+1$, and any origin-symmetric subset $S$ with $\mathrm{ind}(S)\ge k$, we have $S\cap X\ne\varnothing$.

nodes.name: Theorem 7
nodes.statement:
For any weighted graph $G=(V,E,\mu,w)$ satisfying $\mu_v=\sum_{u\in V:u\sim v}w_{uv}$, $\forall v\in V$, for any $p\ge 1$, we have 
$$\frac{2^{p-1}}{p^p}h_{k-\beta}(G)^p\le \lambda_{k}(\Delta_p)\le 2^{p-1} h_k(G).$$

nodes.name: Corollary 4
nodes.statement: For any weighted unicyclic graph $G=(V,E,\mu,w)$ satisfying $\mu_v=\sum_{u\in V:u\sim v}w_{uv}$, $\forall v\in V$, we have $\frac{2^{p-1}}{p^p}h_{k-1}(G)\le \lambda_{k}(\Delta_p)\le 2^{p-1} h_k(G)$.
